Introduction to rminka

Source: vignettes/introduction-to-rminka.Rmd
introduction-to-rminka.Rmd

This document introduces you to rminka basic set of tools, and shows you how to apply them to obtain your desired information. Once you’ve installed, read vignette(“rminka”) to learn more.

- Project Queries

Project-related functions will be illustrated using the Biomarató Tarragona 2025 project.

● mnk_proj_byname()

Initially, only the project name is known, so search for its ID with mnk_proj_byname(). Here we use the query “biomarato 2025”.

prj_names <- mnk_proj_byname("biomarato 2025")

prj_names 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 8
#>      id title      place_id slug  created_at updated_at project_type description
#>   <int> <chr>         <int> <chr> <chr>      <chr>      <chr>        <chr>      
#> 1   417 BioMARató…      244 biom… 2025-03-2… 2026-06-2… collection   "La BioMAR…
#> 2   418 BioMARató…      245 biom… 2025-03-2… 2026-05-0… collection   "La BioMAR…
#> 3   419 BioMARató…      249 biom… 2025-03-2… 2026-05-0… collection   "La BioMAR…
#> 4   420 BioMARató…      248 biom… 2025-03-2… 2026-05-0… collection   "La BioMAR…
#> 5   424 BioMARato…      701 biom… 2025-04-0… 2026-09-0… collection   "Descobre …

# For this example 

prj_names[,c(1:2)]
#> # A tibble: 5 × 2
#>      id title                     
#>   <int> <chr>                     
#> 1   417 BioMARató 2025 (Catalunya)
#> 2   418 BioMARató 2025 (Girona)

#> 4   420 BioMARató 2025 (Barcelona)
#> 5   424 BioMARatona 2025

● mnk_proj_info()

Once the project ID is known, retrieve its details with mnk_proj_info(). The Biomarató Tarragona 2025 project has ID 419.

prj_info <- mnk_proj_info(419)

prj_info

#>      id title               created_at subscrib_users place_id slug  description

Note: To retrieve all project participants, including users who are not subscribed, download observations with mnk_proj_obs() and extract unique user_login values. Each observation includes the observer’s login.

To list participants who contributed observations in a particular month, download that month’s observations and extract unique logins. The example below does this for May 2025:

# 1. Download all observations for the project in may 2025

obs_2025 <- mnk_proj_obs(
  419, year = 2025, month = 5, quiet = TRUE
)

# 2. Extract the unique participants

participants_may_2025 <- obs_2025 %>%
  distinct(user_login) %>%
  arrange(user_login)

participants_may_2025

● mnk_proj_obs()

Returns observations for a project in a selected year and, optionally, month. For project 419, the full year 2025 is retrieved with mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025), or May with mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025, month = 5).

prj_obs <- mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025, month = 5)

- User Queries

User-related functions will be illustrated using the user Xavier Salvador.

● mnk_user_byname()

Initially, only an approximate name is known, so search for the corresponding login. Here, the query “xavi” returns possible logins; select Xavier Salvador from the results.

user_name <- mnk_user_byname("xavi")

- Place Queries

Place-related functions will be illustrated using the place Piscines del Fòrum

● mnk_place_byname()

Initially, only an approximate place name is known, so search for its ID. The query “forum” returns possible places. The place used below is “Piscines del Fòrum” (ID 253); try different search terms if needed.

places <- mnk_place_byname("Forum")

places[,1:6]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   place_id slug                      name     area display_name location_latitud
#>      <int> <chr>                     <chr>   <dbl> <chr>                   <dbl>
#> 1      253 piscinas-del-forum-fecdas Pisc… 4.28e-5 Piscinas de…             41.4
#> 2      257 platja-banys-del-forum    Plat… 1.28e-5 Platja Bany…             41.4
#> 3      820 atles-zona-de-banys-del-… Atle… 9.59e-6 Atles Zona …             41.4

● mnk_place_sf()

Returns the sf geometry for a place. For Piscines del Fòrum, retrieve the geometry with mnk_place_sf(253).

The example maps the geometry with leaflet using the default WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) coordinates. The returned sf object includes the place name.

# 1. Downloading the geometry 

places_forum <- mnk_place_sf(253)

# 2. Drawing the map

 forum_sf <-leaflet(places_forum) %>%
                addProviderTiles("OpenStreetMap", group = "OSM") %>%
                addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satélite") %>%
                addPolygons(
                  color = "#2c4fb8",
                  weight = 2,
                  opacity = 1,
                  fillOpacity = 0.4,
                  label = ~name, # information added from previous function
                  highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
                    weight = 3, bringToFront = TRUE
                  )
                ) %>%
                addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satélite", "OSM"))
 forum_sf

● mnk_place_obs()

Returns observations recorded within a place for a selected year and, optionally, month or day. The result is a data frame without geometry. For Piscines del Fòrum, retrieve February 2025 observations with mnk_place_obs(place_id = 253, year = 2025, month = 2).

Convert the result to an sf object with mnk_obs_sf() and map the points with leaflet.

obs_place <- mnk_place_obs(place_id = 253, year = 2025, month = 2, quiet = TRUE)

obs_place

# Use the packaged sample if the live query returns no observations.
if (nrow(obs_place) == 0) {
  obs_place <- subset(cached_obs, taxon_name %in% c(
    "Diplodus sargus", "Parablennius pilicornis"
  ))
}

# Convert the data frame to an sf object for mapping.
obs_sf <- mnk_obs_sf(obs_place, "id", "taxon_name", "observed_on",
                     "uri", "user_login")

# Prepare text for the marker popup.

popup_final <- paste0(
  "ID: ", obs_sf$id, "<br>",
  "Species: ", obs_sf$taxon_name, "<br>",
  "Observer: ", obs_sf$user_login, "<br>",
  "Date: ", obs_sf$observed_on
)

# Only the observations:

leaflet(obs_sf) %>%
                addProviderTiles("OpenStreetMap", group = "OSM") %>%
                addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satélite") %>%
                addMarkers(lng = ~longitude,
                           lat = ~latitude,
                           popup = popup_final) %>%
                addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satélite", "OSM"))

#  Observations plus place maping

 forum_sf %>%
  addMarkers(data = obs_sf, popup = ~popup_final)

- Observation Queries

● mnk_obs_id()

Retrieves the full record for a known Minka observation ID, including its taxonomic, location, and identification details.

# Retrieve the observation with ID 553028.
obs_id <- mnk_obs_id(id = 553028)

obs_id
#> # A tibble: 1 × 166
#>   quality_grade time_observed_at       taxon_geoprivacy annotations uuid      id

#> 1 research      2025-08-22T12:22:00+0… NA               <list [0]>  b106… 553028
#> # ℹ 160 more variables: cached_votes_total <int>,
#> #   identifications_most_agree <lgl>, species_guess <chr>,
#> #   identifications_most_disagree <lgl>, tags <list>,

#> #   reviewed_by <list>, oauth_application_id <lgl>, flags <list>, …

● mnk_obs()

This is the core function of the package. It supports searches by project, user, place, date, taxon, or geographic area. Two notes apply to mnk_obs() calls:

When a query runs, a message reports the number of matching observations. By default, at most 10,000 records are downloaded. Set limit_download = FALSE to retrieve all matching records.

To retrieve only validated records, use quality = "research". Previous examples covered project, user, and place searches. The following examples show taxon and bounding-box searches.

  1. Taxon search. The following examples search for the genus Raja in 2025 and the species Raja brachyura in 2023.
# Suppress progress messages with `quiet = TRUE`.

# Get 2025 Raja observations for Xavier Salvador (user ID 4).

obs <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Raja", year = 2025, user_id = 4,
  quiet = TRUE, quality = "research"
)

obs # show full dataframe
#> # A tibble: 38 × 29
#>        id observed_on  year month  week   day  hour created_at        updated_at
#>     <int> <chr>       <int> <int> <int> <int> <int> <chr>             <chr>     
#>  1 414056 2025-01-24   2025     1     4    24     0 2025-01-29T10:04… 2025-01-2…
#>  2 427152 2025-02-19   2025     2     8    19    20 2025-03-19T10:19… 2025-03-1…
#>  3 427148 2025-02-19   2025     2     8    19    20 2025-03-19T10:19… 2025-03-2…
#>  4 427142 2025-02-19   2025     2     8    19    20 2025-03-19T10:19… 2025-03-1…
#>  5 427141 2025-02-19   2025     2     8    19    20 2025-03-19T10:19… 2025-03-1…
#>  6 427140 2025-02-19   2025     2     8    19    20 2025-03-19T10:19… 2025-03-1…
#>  7 422169 2025-02-27   2025     2     9    27    20 2025-02-28T11:17… 2025-02-2…
#>  8 420087 2025-02-21   2025     2     8    21    15 2025-02-21T15:14… 2025-02-2…
#>  9 429445 2025-03-27   2025     3    13    27    21 2025-03-30T18:52… 2025-03-3…
#> 10 429443 2025-03-26   2025     3    13    26    21 2025-03-30T18:52… 2025-03-3…
#> # ℹ 28 more rows
#> # ℹ 20 more variables: latitude <dbl>, longitude <dbl>,
#> #   positional_accuracy <int>, geoprivacy <chr>, obscured <lgl>, uri <chr>,
#> #   url_picture_icon <chr>, url_picture_med <chr>, url_picture_orig <chr>,
#> #   quality_grade <chr>, taxon_id <int>, taxon_name <chr>, taxon_rank <chr>,
#> #   taxon_min_ancestry <chr>, taxon_endemic <lgl>, taxon_threatened <lgl>,
#> #   taxon_introduced <lgl>, taxon_native <lgl>, user_id <int>, …

# Get 2023 Raja brachyura observations for Xavier Salvador (user ID 4).

obs_brachyura <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Raja brachyura", year = 2023, user_id = 4,
  quiet = TRUE, quality = "research"
)

obs_brachyura[, intersect(
  c("id", "observed_on", "latitude", "longitude", "taxon_name", "user_login"),
  names(obs_brachyura)
), drop = FALSE]

Observation results include medium- and original-resolution photo URLs when photos are available.

# Get 2022 Raja undulata observations for Xavier Salvador (user ID 4).

obs_undulata <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Raja undulata", year = 2022, user_id = 4,
  quiet = TRUE, quality = "research"
)

# Display the photo URL when the query returns an observation with a photo.
if (nrow(obs_undulata) > 0 &&
    "url_picture_med" %in% names(obs_undulata) &&
    !is.na(obs_undulata$url_picture_med[1])) {
  obs_undulata$url_picture_med[1]
} else {
  message("No observation photo is available for this query.")
}
#> [1] "https://observe.minka-sdg.org/attachments/local_photos/files/65461/medium.jpeg"
  1. Bounding-box search. Retrieve observations within a rectangle by supplying its southwest and northeast corners. The following example searches around Platja de Sant Sebastià in Barcelona with mnk_obs().

# Read the packaged study-area shapefile.

shp_path <- system.file("extdata", "espigo_w.shp", package = "rminka")

espigo <- sf::st_read(shp_path, quiet = TRUE)

# Ensure WGS 84 coordinates for web maps.

bounds <- st_transform(espigo, 4326)

Alternatively, define the area with a vector of coordinates for its corners:

bounds <- c(ymax, xmax, ymin, xmin)

Applied to the Espigo del W example, this would be:

bounds <- c(41.371239, 2.193971, 41.368182, 2.189147)

The map below displays both points with the Espigó del W study area to illustrate the bounds parameter.

#Pmin
xmin <- 2.189147
ymin <- 41.368182

#Pmax
xmax <- 2.193971
ymax <- 41.371239

pts <- data.frame(
  id = c("Pmin", "Pmax"),
  lng = c(xmin, xmax),
  lat = c(ymin, ymax)
)

# Create an interactive map of the study area and its corner points.

bound <- leaflet() %>%
                addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satélite") %>%
                addProviderTiles("OpenStreetMap", group = "OSM") %>%
                addCircleMarkers(             
                         data = pts,
                          radius = 20,
                          color = "cyan",
                          weight = 2,
                          fillOpacity = 0.7,
                          label = ~id,
                          popup = ~paste0("<b>", id, "</b><br>",
                                          "lon: ", round(lng, 6), "<br>",
                                          "lat: ", round(lat, 6))) %>%
                addPolygons(data =    bounds,
                          color = "#2c4fb8",
                          weight = 2,
                          opacity = 1,
                          fillOpacity = 0.4,
                          label = "Bound Espigo W",
                          popup = "Bound Espigo W",
                          highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
                            weight = 3, bringToFront = TRUE
                          )) %>%
                addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satélite", "OSM"))
#> Assuming "lng" and "lat" are longitude and latitude, respectively

bound  # display map in document

# Obtain observations within the study area.

obs_torpedo_bounds <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Torpedo", year = 2024, bounds = bounds,
  quality = "research", quiet = TRUE
)

obs_torpedo_bounds

# Use packaged sample observations if the live query returns no results.
obs_torpedo_example <- obs_torpedo_bounds
if (nrow(obs_torpedo_example) == 0) {
  obs_torpedo_example <- subset(
    cached_obs, taxon_name == "Torpedo torpedo"
  )
}

# Convert the data frame to an sf object and select fields for the map popup.

# Keep observation details for the map popup.
obs_bounds_sf <- mnk_obs_sf(
  obs_torpedo_example, "id", "taxon_name", "observed_on",
  "uri", "user_login", "quality_grade"
)

# Preparing the obtained data for later display in the marker popup

popup_final_torpedo <- paste0(
  "ID: ", obs_bounds_sf$id, "<br>",
  "Species: ", obs_bounds_sf$taxon_name, "<br>",
  "Observer: ", obs_bounds_sf$user_login, "<br>",
  "Date: ", obs_bounds_sf$observed_on
)

# Display the observations on the map.

bound %>%
  addMarkers(data = obs_bounds_sf, popup = ~popup_final_torpedo)

● mnk_obs_byday()

Works like mnk_obs() but uses an explicit date interval. The interval is inclusive and is defined by:

  • d1: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format
  • d2: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format
# Retrieve research-grade Raja undulata observations from January to May 2024.

obs_undulata_2024 <- mnk_obs_byday(
  taxon_name = "Raja undulata",
  d1 = "2024-01-01",
  d2 = "2024-05-25",
  quiet = TRUE,
  quality = "research"
)

- Auxiliary functions

The first two examples use the Torpedo torpedo observations from the Espigó del W study area above. The remaining examples use other data.

● mnk_obs_sf()

This function converts an observation data frame into an sf point layer. It uses the latitude and longitude columns returned by mnk_obs() and other observation functions. The default CRS is EPSG:4326 (WGS 84); set crs to use another coordinate system. The example below uses Torpedo torpedo observations from the Espigó del W study area.

# Convert the observations to a projected sf layer.
obs_utm <- mnk_obs_sf(
  obs_torpedo_example, id, taxon_name, observed_on, user_login,
  quality_grade, uri, crs = 25831
)

# The function retains the selected attributes and adds the geometry.

# `crs = 25831` requests ETRS89 / UTM zone 31N, a projected CRS useful
# for distance calculations and local Catalan cartography.


# Leaflet uses Web Mercator by default. To map UTM data, change the base CRS.

crs25831 <- leafletCRS(
  crsClass = "L.Proj.CRS",
  code = "EPSG:25831",
  proj4def = "+proj=utm +zone=31 +ellps=GRS80 +units=m +no_defs",
  resolutions = c(
    8192, 4096, 2048, 1024, 512, 256, 128, 64,
    32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, 0.5
  ),
  origin = c(0, 9000000)
)

# This map uses the ICGC WMS because standard OSM tiles do not use this CRS.

leaflet(options = leafletOptions(crs25831, minZoom = 0, maxZoom = 14)) %>%
  
      addWMSTiles(
        "https://geoserveis.icgc.cat/servei/catalunya/mapa-base/wms",
        layers = "orto",
        options = WMSTileOptions(format = "image/png", 
          transparent = TRUE, version = "1.3.0"
        )
      ) %>%
    
# Display observation details in the map popup.
      addCircleMarkers(
        data = obs_utm,
        radius = 6,
        color = "red",
        fillOpacity = 0.9,
        popup = paste0(
          "ID: ", obs_utm$id, "<br>",
          "Species: ", obs_utm$taxon_name, "<br>",
          "Observer: ", obs_utm$user_login, "<br>",
          "Quality: ", obs_utm$quality_grade, "<br>",
          "Date: ", obs_utm$observed_on
        )
      )

● export_mnk_qgis()

This function writes sf objects to a GeoPackage (.gpkg), creating one layer per object. It supports GIS workflows such as QGIS by validating geometries, dropping Z/M dimensions, removing unsupported list-columns, and transforming features to the target CRS.

We will apply it to the observation layer created above.

output_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".gpkg")
export_mnk_qgis(observations = obs_utm, file = output_file)
unlink(output_file)

# The output path is temporary, so the example does not create a file in the
# package source directory.
#
# Multiple named sf objects can also be exported as separate GeoPackage layers:

# * places_forum: a polygon defining the Forum pools area, saved as layer "zone"

# * obs_sf: point observations from the Forum pools, saved as layer
#   "observations"
# Both layers can be written to the same GeoPackage file.

● get_wrm_tax()

This function retrieves taxonomic information from the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS) for a scientific name. The examples show how to retrieve taxonomy for a single species and how to combine taxonomic information with observations returned by an observation function. The WoRMS response includes habitat flags, such as marine, brackish-water, freshwater, and terrestrial status, as well as an extinct flag.

# Retrieve taxonomy for a single species

get_wrm_tax("Diplodus sargus")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   valid_AphiaID valid_name      rank    kingdom  phylum class order family genus
#>           <int> <chr>           <chr>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr> <chr> <chr>  <chr>
#> 1        127053 Diplodus sargus Species Animalia Chord… Tele… Eupe… Spari… Dipl…
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: isMarine <lgl>, isBrackish <lgl>, isFreshwater <lgl>,
#> #   isTerrestrial <lgl>, isExtinct <lgl>

# Retrieve taxonomy for each species in the previous observation data.

unique_taxa <- obs_place %>%
  filter(!is.na(taxon_name)) %>%
  distinct(taxon_name) %>%
  pull(taxon_name)

taxonomy_df <- map_dfr(
  setNames(unique_taxa, unique_taxa),
  ~ get_wrm_tax(.x),
  .id = "taxon_name"
)
#> WoRMS API request failed. Status code: 500
#> No taxon found for the scientific name: 'Life'.
#> No taxon found for the scientific name: 'Ichthyaetus audouinii'.

# Join the taxonomic information to the observation data.
obs_place_tax <- obs_place %>%
  left_join(taxonomy_df, by = "taxon_name")

● shrt_name()

This function creates a standardized abbreviation from a scientific name. The example uses abbreviations to plot observation frequencies from obs_place.

# Create standardized abbreviations for scientific names.

obs_place <- obs_place %>%
  mutate(
    shrt_tax_name = map_chr(taxon_name, ~ {
      if (is.na(.x) || .x == "") NA_character_ else shrt_name(.x)
    })
  )
  
# Count observations per abbreviated species and keep the top 10.

freq_top10 <- obs_place %>%
  filter(!is.na(shrt_tax_name)) %>%          # remove missing names
  count(shrt_tax_name, name = "n_obs") %>%    # count occurrences
  slice_max(n_obs, n = 10) %>%                # keep the 10 most frequent
  arrange(n_obs)   

# Plot a horizontal bar chart of observation frequency.

ggplot(freq_top10, aes(x = n_obs, y = reorder(shrt_tax_name, n_obs))) +
        geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
        geom_text(aes(label = n_obs), hjust = -0.2, size = 2) +
        scale_x_continuous(
          expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
        ) +
        labs(
              x = "Number of observations",
              y = "Species (abbreviated)",
              title = "Observation frequency",
              subtitle = " Forum February 2025"
            ) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
